pairnote.document>document: Text, headings, lists, tables and images are carried over; page layout is recalculated where the target is reflowable (Markdown, HTML, EPUB).
pairnote.document>ebook: Chapters come from the headings and a table of contents is generated; fonts are left to the reader device.
pairnote.document>image: Every page becomes one image (a multi-page document gives one image per page, packed in a ZIP); resolution defaults to 150 dpi.
pairnote.document>vector: Pages become vector graphics: text and lines stay sharp at any zoom.
pairnote.document>spreadsheet: Each record becomes a row and each field a column; nested values are flattened into column names like address.city.
pairnote.spreadsheet>spreadsheet: Sheets, formulas, number formats and merged cells are kept between Excel and OpenDocument; CSV keeps only the values of the active sheet.
pairnote.spreadsheet>document: The sheet is laid out as a table; formulas are exported as their current values.
pairnote.spreadsheet>image: The printable area of the sheet becomes an image.
pairnote.presentation>presentation: Slides, layouts, speaker notes and images are kept; transitions and animations are kept where the target supports them.
pairnote.presentation>document: Every slide becomes one page; to Word you get a handout with the slide picture, text and notes.
pairnote.presentation>image: Every slide becomes one image (a ZIP for several slides).
pairnote.presentation>video: Each slide is shown for 3 seconds by default (adjustable) in a Full HD video.
pairnote.ebook>ebook: Text, chapters, table of contents, cover and metadata are kept; layout is adapted to the target device profile.
pairnote.ebook>document: The book's text and chapters are carried over; DRM-protected books can't be converted.
pairnote.image>image: Pixels, transparency (where the target has it), colour profile and EXIF data are kept unless you choose to strip metadata.
pairnote.image>document: The image is placed on a page at its own size and resolution.
pairnote.image>vector: The image is traced into vector paths (Potrace): best for logos, icons and line art, not for photos.
pairnote.image>video: The animation frames become a video with the original timing.
pairnote.vector>vector: Paths, text and colours stay vector; effects the target can't store are rasterised.
pairnote.vector>image: The drawing is rendered at 150 dpi by default; set a width for a sharper or smaller image.
pairnote.vector>document: The drawing becomes a vector PDF page: it stays sharp when printed.
pairnote.video>video: Video and audio are re-encoded for the target container; resolution and frame rate stay the same unless you change them.
pairnote.video>audio: The audio track is extracted and encoded; the picture is dropped.
pairnote.video>image: A GIF, WebP or APNG animation is made at 12 fps and 480 px width by default; JPG or PNG gives one frame.
pairnote.audio>audio: Sample rate and channels are kept unless you change them; lossy targets use the default bitrate below.
pairnote.audio>video: The sound gets a still picture (black by default, or a cover you choose) so it can be uploaded to video sites.
pairnote.archive>archive: The files and folders are unpacked and repacked; a password can be given for the source and for the new archive.
pairnote.cad>cad: Entities, layers and blocks are carried over; DWG writing is experimental in LibreDWG, so check the result in your CAD program.
pairnote.cad>vector: The model space is drawn with layer colours and line types as vectors.
pairnote.cad>image: The model space is rendered on white at 200 dpi by default.
pairnote.cad>document: The model space becomes a vector PDF page.
pairnote.font>font: Glyphs, metrics, kerning and names are kept; TrueType and CFF outlines are converted when the target needs the other kind.

fmt.lzo: LZO is a single file compressed with lzop.
fmt.z: Z is a single file compressed with Unix compress.
fmt.cab: CAB is the Microsoft Cabinet archive of Windows installers.
fmt.iso: ISO is a CD/DVD disc image.
fmt.img: IMG is a raw disk image.
fmt.dmg: DMG is a macOS disk image.
fmt.war: WAR is a Java web application archive.
fmt.apk: APK is an Android app package.
fmt.deb: DEB is a Debian / Ubuntu software package.
fmt.rpm: RPM is a Red Hat / Fedora software package.
fmt.cpio: CPIO is an old Unix archive, used in Linux initramfs.
fmt.arj: ARJ is an old DOS-era archive.
fmt.lha: LHA (LZH) is a Japanese archive format popular on the Amiga.
fmt.ace: ACE is an old Windows archive format.
fmt.alz: ALZ is the ALZip archive from Korea.
fmt.arc: ARC is one of the first PC archive formats.
fmt.wim: WIM is the Windows imaging format of installers.
fmt.dwg: DWG is AutoCAD's native drawing format and the most common CAD file.
fmt.dxf: DXF is Autodesk's open drawing exchange format that most CAD programs read.
fmt.ttf: TTF (TrueType) is the most widely supported desktop font format.
fmt.otf: OTF (OpenType) is a font with advanced typography (ligatures, small caps).
fmt.woff: WOFF is a compressed web font.
fmt.woff2: WOFF2 is the most compact web font, supported by all modern browsers.
fmt.eot: EOT is the web font of old Internet Explorer versions.
fmt.ttc: TTC is a TrueType collection with several fonts in one file.
fmt.pfb: PFB is a PostScript Type 1 font (binary).
fmt.pfa: PFA is a PostScript Type 1 font (text).
fmt.sfd: SFD is FontForge's editable font source.
fmt.dfont: DFONT is an old macOS font suitcase.
fmt.bdf: BDF is a bitmap font of the X Window System.

page_range.label: Pages

ocr.label: OCR
ocr.help: Recognise text in scanned PDFs (auto: only when the PDF has no text layer).

ocr_language.label: OCR language
ocr_language.help: Tesseract language codes, e.g. eng, hun or hun+eng.

title.label: Title
title.help: Book or document title written into the metadata.

output_profile.label: Device
output_profile.help: E-book device profile: Kindle, Kobo, tablet…

delimiter.label: CSV delimiter
delimiter.help: Auto detects comma, semicolon or tab.

seconds_per_slide.label: Seconds per slide
seconds_per_slide.help: How long each slide is shown in the video (0.5–60).

width.label: Width (px)
width.help: New width; with only width set, the height follows the aspect ratio.

height.label: Height (px)
height.help: New height; with only height set, the width follows the aspect ratio.

fit.label: Fit
fit.help: inside: within the box · cover: fill and crop · contain: pad · fill: stretch.

quality.label: Quality
quality.help: 1–100; lower is smaller. JPG default 88, WebP 85, AVIF 70.

strip_metadata.label: Remove metadata
strip_metadata.help: Drop EXIF (camera, GPS location, date) and other metadata.

background.label: Background
background.help: Colour behind transparent areas, e.g. #ffffff or white.

lossless.label: Lossless
lossless.help: WebP / JPEG XL without quality loss.

video_codec.label: Video codec
video_codec.help: auto, H.264, H.265, VP9, AV1, MPEG-4, MPEG-2, ProRes, copy (no re-encoding).

audio_codec.label: Audio codec
audio_codec.help: auto, AAC, MP3, Opus, Vorbis, FLAC, PCM, AC3, copy, none.

aspect_mode.label: Aspect mode
aspect_mode.help: pad with black bars, crop, or stretch.

preset.label: Encoding speed
preset.help: Slower presets give smaller files at the same quality.

start.label: Start
start.help: Cut from here: seconds or hh:mm:ss.

end.label: End
end.help: Cut until here: seconds or hh:mm:ss.

subtitles.label: Subtitles
subtitles.help: An uploaded SRT, VTT or ASS file (file_id).

subtitles_mode.label: Subtitle mode
subtitles_mode.help: burn into the picture, or add as a switchable track.

at.label: Frame at
at.help: Time of the frame for JPG/PNG from video, in seconds.

password.label: Password
password.help: For opening a protected source, or for encrypting the result (ZIP, 7Z).

font_index.label: Font index
font_index.help: Which font of a collection (TTC), from 0.

subset_text.label: Only these characters
subset_text.help: Keep only the glyphs of this text (smaller web font).

text_to_path.label: Text to paths
text_to_path.help: Turn text into outlines (no fonts needed to open).

advanced.label: Advanced parameters
advanced.help: Allow-listed FFmpeg or ImageMagick flags, e.g. -tune film or -sharpen 0x1.

frame.label: Frame / layer
frame.help: Which frame of an animation or multi-page image, from 0.

max_width.label: Maximum width
max_width.help: Shrink wider images to this width.

target_size_mb.label: Target size (MB)
target_size_mb.help: Aim for this file size; bitrate is calculated from the length.

page_ranges.label: Page ranges
page_ranges.help: One range per file, e.g. 1-3, all, 2.

mode.label: Split mode
mode.help: ranges, every N pages, or each page separately.

every.label: Every N pages
every.help: Pages per part when splitting evenly.

expand.label: Grow canvas
expand.help: Enlarge the canvas so nothing is cut off.

margins_mm.label: Margins (mm)
margins_mm.help: top, right, bottom, left to cut off.

page_size.label: Page size
page_size.help: A3, A4, A5, B5, Letter, Legal, Tabloid.

what.label: Flatten
what.help: all, only form fields, or only annotations.

words.label: Words
words.help: Words or phrases to black out.

position.label: Position
position.help: Where to place it on the page or picture.

percent.label: Percent
percent.help: Scale by percent instead of pixels.

box.label: Area
box.help: x, y, width, height in pixels.

image_file.label: Logo image
image_file.help: An uploaded image used as the watermark (file_id).

rotation.label: Rotation
rotation.help: Degrees, e.g. 45 for a diagonal watermark.

audio_format.label: Audio format
audio_format.help: mp3, m4a, wav, flac, ogg, opus, aac.

loops.label: Repeats
loops.help: How many times the animation plays in the video.

burn.label: Burn in
burn.help: Burn the subtitles into the picture (otherwise a switchable track).

language.label: Language
language.help: Language of the content, e.g. Hungarian.

full_page.label: Whole page
full_page.help: Capture the full scrolling page, not only the screen.

wait_ms.label: Wait (ms)
wait_ms.help: Extra time for the page to finish loading.

archive_format.label: Archive format
archive_format.help: zip, 7z, tar, tar.gz, tar.bz2, tar.xz, tar.zst.

keep_look.label: Keep the original look
keep_look.help: Fill on the original page (for photos and scans) instead of a clean rebuild.

flatten.label: Flatten
flatten.help: Bake the values in for printing.

data_file.label: Data table
data_file.help: CSV or XLSX: one filled copy per row.

placement.label: Placement
placement.help: auto (signature field or line), field, xy, anchor.

source_files.label: Source documents
source_files.help: Documents to take answers from (ID card, invoice…).

answers.label: Answers
answers.help: Answers to the questions the assistant asked.

cover.label: Cover
cover.help: An uploaded image (file_id) as cover or still picture.

sheet.label: Sheet

compress-pdf.name: Compress PDF
compress-pdf.title: Compress PDF — make PDF files smaller online, free
compress-pdf.desc: Shrink PDF files with Ghostscript: three levels from print quality to smallest. Text stays selectable.
compress-pdf.intro: Compress PDF reduces the size of a PDF by re-compressing its images and fonts with Ghostscript: “recommended” resamples pictures to 150 dpi, “extreme” to 72 dpi, “low” keeps 300 dpi for print. Text, links and bookmarks stay intact; files up to {guest_mb} MB are free without an account.
points: Three levels: low (300 dpi), recommended (150 dpi), extreme (72 dpi)
Several PDFs at once with the same setting
faq: How much smaller will my PDF get?
PDFs with photos or scans usually shrink by 50–90%; text-only PDFs are already small and change little.

compress-image.name: Compress image
compress-image.title: Compress images — JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC smaller online
compress-image.desc: Reduce image file size: set the quality, a maximum width, and remove EXIF data. Up to {max_files} images at once.
compress-image.intro: Compress images re-encodes photos and graphics at a lower, still sharp quality (JPG/WebP 80 by default), can limit the width and removes EXIF data such as GPS location. Up to {max_files} images at once; the format stays the same.
points: Removes camera and location data on request

compress-jpeg.name: Compress JPEG
compress-jpeg.title: Compress JPEG — smaller JPG photos online
compress-jpeg.desc: Make JPG photos smaller with progressive encoding and adjustable quality.
compress-jpeg.intro: Compress JPEG re-encodes JPG photos as optimised, progressive JPEGs at quality 80 by default — typically 40–70% smaller with no visible difference. Metadata can be removed.

compress-png.name: Compress PNG
compress-png.title: Compress PNG — smaller PNG images online
compress-png.desc: Shrink PNG images with palette quantisation while keeping transparency.
compress-png.intro: Compress PNG reduces the colours to an optimised palette (256 by default) and recompresses the file; transparency is kept. Screenshots and graphics typically shrink by 50–80%.

compress-gif.name: Compress GIF
compress-gif.title: Compress GIF — smaller animated GIFs
compress-gif.desc: Make animated GIFs smaller: fewer colours, lower frame rate, smaller width.
compress-gif.intro: Compress GIF rebuilds the animation with an optimised palette, and can reduce the frame rate and width — the main levers of GIF size.

compress-video.name: Compress video
compress-video.title: Compress video — MP4, MOV, MKV smaller online
compress-video.desc: Shrink videos with H.264 or H.265: choose a quality (CRF), a resolution or a target size in MB.
compress-video.intro: Compress video re-encodes the video with H.264 at CRF 28 by default (H.265 on request), optionally at a lower resolution, or aims for a file size you set in MB. Phone videos often shrink by 60–80%.

compress-mp3.name: Compress MP3
compress-mp3.title: Compress MP3 — smaller audio files
compress-mp3.desc: Reduce the bitrate of MP3 and other audio files; mono for speech.
compress-mp3.intro: Compress MP3 re-encodes audio at a lower bitrate (96 kbit/s by default) and can make it mono — enough for speech and podcasts, about a third of a 320 kbit/s file.

compress-wav.name: Compress WAV
compress-wav.title: Compress WAV — smaller uncompressed audio
compress-wav.desc: Make WAV files smaller by lowering the sample rate, channels or bit depth.
compress-wav.intro: Compress WAV keeps the file uncompressed and lossless in format but lowers the sample rate (e.g. 48 → 22.05 kHz), the channels or the bit depth. For the smallest lossless file convert to FLAC instead.

merge-pdf.name: Merge PDF
merge-pdf.title: Merge PDF — combine up to {max_files} files into one PDF
merge-pdf.desc: Combine PDFs, Word files and images into one PDF in the order you choose; up to {max_files} files.
merge-pdf.intro: Merge PDF joins up to {max_files} files into one PDF in the order you upload them. Word, PowerPoint and image files are converted to PDF first, and for each file you can take only some pages (e.g. 1-3).
points: Mix PDFs, Word files and images

split-pdf.name: Split PDF
split-pdf.title: Split PDF — by page ranges, every N pages or every page
split-pdf.desc: Split a PDF into several files: by ranges, every N pages, or one file per page. Delivered as a ZIP.
split-pdf.intro: Split PDF cuts a document into parts: by page ranges you list (1-3,4-10), into equal parts of N pages, or into single pages. The parts come in a ZIP.

extract-pages.name: Extract PDF pages
extract-pages.title: Extract pages from a PDF
extract-pages.desc: Save chosen pages of a PDF as a new PDF.
extract-pages.intro: Extract pages makes a new PDF from the pages you list (e.g. 2,5-7), in that order; the original stays unchanged.

delete-pdf-pages.name: Delete PDF pages
delete-pdf-pages.title: Delete pages from a PDF
delete-pdf-pages.desc: Remove pages from a PDF by number or range.
delete-pdf-pages.intro: Delete pages removes the pages you list (e.g. 1,4-6) and saves the rest as a new PDF.

rotate-pdf.name: Rotate PDF
rotate-pdf.title: Rotate PDF pages — all or selected
rotate-pdf.desc: Rotate all or selected PDF pages by 90, 180 or 270 degrees, permanently.
rotate-pdf.intro: Rotate PDF turns all pages, or only the ones you list, by 90, 180 or 270 degrees and saves the rotation in the file.

organize-pdf.name: Organise PDF
organize-pdf.title: Organise PDF — reorder pages
organize-pdf.desc: Put PDF pages in a new order, duplicate or drop them.
organize-pdf.intro: Organise PDF rebuilds the document in the page order you give (e.g. 3,1,2,4-); pages left out are dropped, listed twice are duplicated.

crop-pdf.name: Crop PDF
crop-pdf.title: Crop PDF margins
crop-pdf.desc: Cut the margins of PDF pages in millimetres.
crop-pdf.intro: Crop PDF trims the margins you give in millimetres (top, right, bottom, left) from all or selected pages.

resize-pdf.name: Resize PDF
resize-pdf.title: Resize PDF pages — A4, Letter, A5 and more
resize-pdf.desc: Change the page size of a PDF to A3, A4, A5, Letter or Legal.
resize-pdf.intro: Resize PDF places every page on a new paper size (A4 by default), scaled to fit, to fill or stretched.

pdf-to-pdfa.name: PDF to PDF/A
pdf-to-pdfa.title: Convert PDF to PDF/A for archiving
pdf-to-pdfa.desc: Make an ISO PDF/A-1b, 2b or 3b file with Ghostscript: fonts embedded, sRGB colour profile.
pdf-to-pdfa.intro: PDF to PDF/A produces an archival PDF/A-2b file by default (1b and 3b available): all fonts are embedded and an sRGB output intent is added, as courts and public archives require.

pdf-to-pdfx.name: PDF to PDF/X
pdf-to-pdfx.title: Convert PDF to PDF/X for print
pdf-to-pdfx.desc: Prepare a print-ready PDF/X file with Ghostscript.
pdf-to-pdfx.intro: PDF to PDF/X makes a print-oriented PDF/X-3 file with embedded fonts and a defined output intent.

ocr-pdf.name: OCR PDF
ocr-pdf.title: OCR PDF — make scanned PDFs searchable
ocr-pdf.desc: Add an invisible text layer to scanned PDFs and photos with Tesseract OCR; Hungarian and 100+ languages.
ocr-pdf.intro: OCR PDF recognises the text of scanned pages with Tesseract and adds it as an invisible layer, so the PDF becomes searchable and copyable while looking the same. Crooked pages are straightened first.

protect-pdf.name: Protect PDF
protect-pdf.title: Protect PDF with a password and permissions
protect-pdf.desc: Encrypt a PDF with AES-256, set an open password and permissions for printing, copying and editing.
protect-pdf.intro: Protect PDF encrypts the file with AES-256: an open password is needed to read it, and a separate permissions password controls printing, copying, editing and comments.

unlock-pdf.name: Unlock PDF
unlock-pdf.title: Unlock PDF — remove a password you know
unlock-pdf.desc: Remove the password and restrictions from a PDF when you know the password.
unlock-pdf.intro: Unlock PDF removes the encryption and permission restrictions from a PDF whose password you know; without the password it can't be opened.

flatten-pdf.name: Flatten PDF
flatten-pdf.title: Flatten PDF — bake in form fields and comments
flatten-pdf.desc: Make filled form fields and annotations part of the page so they can't be changed.
flatten-pdf.intro: Flatten PDF bakes form field values and annotations into the page content: the result prints and looks the same everywhere and can't be edited. Accented text (ő, ű) stays correct.

extract-pdf-images.name: Extract images from PDF
extract-pdf-images.title: Extract images from a PDF
extract-pdf-images.desc: Save every picture embedded in a PDF in its original quality, as a ZIP.
extract-pdf-images.intro: Extract images saves the pictures embedded in a PDF at their original resolution and format (JPG, PNG…) in a ZIP; tiny decorations are skipped.

annotate-pdf.name: Annotate PDF
annotate-pdf.title: Annotate PDF — highlights, notes and shapes
annotate-pdf.desc: Add highlights, sticky notes, text boxes, rectangles and lines to a PDF.
annotate-pdf.intro: Annotate PDF adds standard PDF annotations — highlight, note, text box, rectangle, line — that every PDF reader shows and that can be flattened later.

edit-pdf.name: Edit PDF
edit-pdf.title: Edit PDF — add text, images and white-out
edit-pdf.desc: Add text and images to PDF pages, cover parts with white, or open the full PDF editor.
edit-pdf.intro: Edit PDF places new text (with accents) and images on the pages and can cover areas with white; for rewriting the existing text open the full PDF editor of the app.

redact-pdf.name: Redact PDF
redact-pdf.title: Redact PDF — permanently black out text
redact-pdf.desc: Black out words and patterns (e-mails, phone numbers, card numbers) permanently.
redact-pdf.intro: Redact PDF finds the words and patterns you give, removes the text under them permanently and draws black boxes — not just a cover that can be lifted.

page-numbers.name: Add page numbers
page-numbers.title: Add page numbers to a PDF
page-numbers.desc: Number PDF pages at the position and in the format you choose.
page-numbers.h1: Add page numbers to a PDF
page-numbers.intro: Add page numbers writes a number on each page — bottom centre by default, or any corner — in a format like “{n}” or “Page {n} of {total}”.

compare-pdf.name: Compare PDF
compare-pdf.title: Compare two PDFs — see what changed
compare-pdf.desc: Compare two versions of a PDF and get a report of the differences.
compare-pdf.intro: Compare PDF puts two versions side by side and marks inserted, deleted and changed text, page by page.

resize-image.name: Resize image
resize-image.title: Resize images — pixels or percent, up to {max_files} at once
resize-image.desc: Resize JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC and other images by pixels or percent; keep or change the aspect ratio.
resize-image.intro: Resize image sets a new width, height or percentage with high-quality Lanczos resampling; fit, cover (crop) or pad keeps the proportions as you choose. Up to {max_files} images at once.

crop-image.name: Crop image
crop-image.title: Crop images — to an area or an aspect ratio
crop-image.desc: Crop pictures to a pixel area or to an aspect ratio like 1:1, 4:5 or 16:9.
crop-image.intro: Crop image cuts a pixel area (x, y, width, height) or the largest centred area of an aspect ratio such as 1:1 for profile pictures or 9:16 for stories.

rotate-image.name: Rotate image
rotate-image.title: Rotate images by 90, 180 or 270 degrees
rotate-image.desc: Rotate pictures permanently, several at once.
rotate-image.intro: Rotate image turns pictures by 90, 180 or 270 degrees and saves the pixels rotated (not only an EXIF flag), so every program shows them right.

flip-image.name: Flip image
flip-image.title: Flip images horizontally or vertically
flip-image.desc: Mirror pictures left–right or upside down.
flip-image.intro: Flip image mirrors pictures horizontally (left–right) or vertically (upside down), several at once.

upscale-image.name: Upscale image
upscale-image.title: Upscale images 2×, 3× or 4×
upscale-image.desc: Enlarge pictures 2–4 times with Lanczos resampling and sharpening.
upscale-image.intro: Upscale image enlarges pictures 2, 3 or 4 times with Lanczos resampling and gentle sharpening — good for small logos and screenshots.

collage-maker.name: Collage maker
collage-maker.title: Collage maker — combine photos into one image
collage-maker.desc: Arrange up to {max_files} photos in a grid with gaps and a background colour.
collage-maker.intro: Collage maker arranges your photos in a balanced grid (columns automatic or chosen), with the gap and background colour you set, as one JPG.

color-picker.name: Colour picker
color-picker.title: Image colour picker — the main colours of a picture
color-picker.desc: Get the dominant colours of an image as HEX and RGB values.
color-picker.intro: Colour picker finds the dominant colours of a picture (8 by default) and lists them with HEX, RGB and their share of the image — handy for brand palettes.

trim-video.name: Trim video
trim-video.title: Trim video — cut the start and end online
trim-video.desc: Cut a video to the part you need by start and end time.
trim-video.intro: Trim video keeps the part between the start and end you give (seconds or hh:mm:ss) and re-encodes it so the cut is frame-accurate.

crop-video.name: Crop video
crop-video.title: Crop video — to 9:16, 1:1, 16:9 or an area
crop-video.desc: Crop a video to an aspect ratio for Reels, TikTok or YouTube, or to a pixel area.
crop-video.intro: Crop video cuts the picture to an aspect ratio (9:16 for Reels and TikTok, 1:1, 4:5, 16:9) centred, or to an exact pixel area.

resize-video.name: Resize video
resize-video.title: Resize video — 4K, 1080p, 720p and more
resize-video.desc: Change the resolution of a video, with bars or cropping for a new aspect ratio.
resize-video.intro: Resize video scales the video to a resolution (1080p, 720p, custom) and, for a different aspect ratio, adds bars or crops.

rotate-video.name: Rotate video
rotate-video.title: Rotate or flip a video
rotate-video.desc: Turn a sideways video by 90, 180 or 270 degrees, or mirror it.
rotate-video.intro: Rotate video fixes sideways phone videos by turning the picture 90, 180 or 270 degrees, and can mirror it.

mute-video.name: Mute video
mute-video.title: Remove audio from a video
mute-video.desc: Make a silent copy of a video without re-encoding the picture.
mute-video.intro: Mute video removes the sound track; the picture is copied unchanged, so it's quick and lossless.

video-to-gif.name: Video to GIF
video-to-gif.title: Video to GIF — make GIFs from MP4, MOV, WebM
video-to-gif.desc: Turn a part of a video into an animated GIF with an optimised palette.
video-to-gif.intro: Video to GIF converts the part you choose (start, end) to an animated GIF at 12 fps and 480 px width by default, with a palette computed from the clip so colours stay clean.

gif-to-video.name: GIF to MP4
gif-to-video.title: GIF to MP4 — animated GIF to video
gif-to-video.desc: Turn GIF, WebP or APNG animations into a small MP4 video.
gif-to-video.intro: GIF to MP4 turns an animation into an H.264 video that is usually 5–10 times smaller and plays everywhere; it can repeat the loop several times.

extract-audio.name: Extract audio
extract-audio.title: Extract audio from video — MP3, M4A, WAV
extract-audio.desc: Save the sound of a video as MP3, M4A, WAV, FLAC or another audio format.
extract-audio.intro: Extract audio saves the sound track of a video as MP3 (192 kbit/s by default) or M4A, WAV, FLAC, OGG, Opus.

add-subtitles.name: Add subtitles
add-subtitles.title: Add subtitles to a video — SRT, VTT, ASS
add-subtitles.desc: Burn subtitles into a video or add them as a switchable track.
add-subtitles.intro: Add subtitles takes a video and an SRT, VTT or ASS file and burns the text into the picture (visible everywhere) or adds a switchable subtitle track.

trim-audio.name: Trim audio
trim-audio.title: Trim audio — cut MP3, WAV, M4A online
trim-audio.desc: Cut audio by start and end time, with fade in and fade out.
trim-audio.intro: Trim audio keeps the part between the start and end you give, with optional fade-in and fade-out, in the same format.

adjust-volume.name: Change volume
adjust-volume.title: Change the volume of audio or video
adjust-volume.desc: Make audio louder or quieter, or normalise loudness to EBU R128.
adjust-volume.intro: Change volume multiplies the level (e.g. 1.5×) or adds decibels (+3 dB), or normalises loudness to the EBU R128 broadcast standard.

watermark-pdf.name: Watermark PDF
watermark-pdf.title: Watermark PDF — text or logo
watermark-pdf.desc: Put a text or logo watermark on every PDF page: position, opacity, rotation.
watermark-pdf.intro: Watermark PDF places a text (accents included) or a logo on every page, centred and diagonal by default, at 30% opacity.

watermark-image.name: Watermark image
watermark-image.title: Watermark images — text or logo, many at once
watermark-image.desc: Add a text or logo watermark to up to {max_files} pictures at once.
watermark-image.intro: Watermark image adds the same text or logo to up to {max_files} pictures, at the position and opacity you choose.

watermark-video.desc: Put a text or logo on a video in any corner.

website-to-pdf.name: Website to PDF
website-to-pdf.title: Website to PDF — save a web page as PDF
website-to-pdf.desc: Save any public web page as a PDF with a real browser (Chromium).
website-to-pdf.intro: Website to PDF opens the page in Chromium, waits for it to load and prints it to PDF on the paper size you choose.

website-to-image.name: Website screenshot
website-to-image.title: Website screenshot — full page PNG or JPG
website-to-image.desc: Capture a web page as a full-length PNG, JPG or WebP image.

merge-files.name: Merge files
merge-files.title: Merge files — PDFs, images, videos or audio into one
merge-files.desc: Join up to {max_files} files into one: PDFs and documents into a PDF, videos into one video, audio into one track.
merge-files.intro: Merge files joins up to {max_files} files of one kind: documents and images into one PDF, video clips into one video, audio files into one track, in upload order.

thumbnail.name: Thumbnail maker
thumbnail.title: Thumbnail maker — preview images of documents, videos, images
thumbnail.desc: Make a preview image of the first page of a document, a frame of a video, or a picture.
thumbnail.intro: Thumbnail maker renders the first page (or the page you choose) of a document, a frame of a video, or a picture as a PNG, JPG or WebP thumbnail, 400 px wide by default.

create-archive.name: Create archive
create-archive.title: Create ZIP or 7Z archive online — with password
create-archive.desc: Pack up to {max_files} files into ZIP, 7Z or TAR.GZ, optionally encrypted with a password.

extract-archive.name: Extract archive
extract-archive.title: Extract RAR, 7Z, ZIP and 40+ archives online
extract-archive.desc: Unpack RAR, 7Z, TAR.GZ, ISO and other archives, also with a password.
extract-archive.intro: Extract archive unpacks 40+ formats (RAR, 7Z, ZIP, TAR.GZ, ISO, CAB, DMG…) with 7-Zip or The Unarchiver and gives you the files, in a ZIP if there are several. Unsafe paths are refused.

read-metadata.name: Metadata viewer
read-metadata.title: Metadata viewer — EXIF, GPS, document properties
read-metadata.desc: Read EXIF, GPS, camera, author and document metadata of any file with ExifTool.
read-metadata.intro: Metadata viewer shows everything ExifTool can read from a file: camera and lens, GPS location, dates, author, software, PDF and Office properties.

edit-metadata.name: Edit metadata
edit-metadata.title: Edit metadata — title, author, date, copyright
edit-metadata.desc: Write title, author, copyright and other metadata into images, videos, PDFs and Office files.

fill-form.title: Fill forms online — PDF, Word, Excel, photo
fill-form.desc: Fill any form and get it back in its original format; accents (ő, ű) stay correct.

bulk-fill-form.name: Bulk fill
bulk-fill-form.title: Bulk fill forms from Excel or CSV
bulk-fill-form.desc: One filled copy of a form per row of a spreadsheet, combined into one file.

make-fillable.name: Make PDF fillable
make-fillable.title: Make a PDF fillable — add real form fields
make-fillable.desc: Turn a printed or scanned form into a fillable PDF with real fields.
make-fillable.intro: Make fillable finds the lines, boxes and tick boxes of a printed form and puts real PDF form fields on them; photos and scans are rebuilt first.

create-signature.name: Create signature
create-signature.title: Create a signature — draw, photograph or upload
create-signature.desc: Draw your signature or initials, or take a photo of one on paper; we make a clean, transparent image and keep it encrypted.
create-signature.intro: Create signature turns a drawing, a photo or a scan of your signature into a clean, transparent PNG (paper, shadow and noise removed) and stores it encrypted, only for you, to reuse on documents.

sign-document.name: Sign document
sign-document.title: Sign PDF and Word documents with your signature
sign-document.desc: Place your saved signature into a signature field or at a chosen spot of a PDF or DOCX.
sign-document.intro: Sign document puts your saved signature into the document's signature field, on the signature line it finds, or exactly where you say — in PDF and Word files.

ai-form-filler.name: AI form filler
ai-form-filler.title: AI form filler — fills forms from your data and documents
ai-form-filler.desc: An assistant fills forms from your profile and uploaded documents, asks what's missing and checks dates, IBANs and Hungarian IDs.

cloudconvert.name: CloudConvert
cloudconvert.desc: A broad conversion API; {product} adds AI editing, forms, signatures and MCP.
cloudconvert.intro: CloudConvert is a well-known conversion service with a jobs-and-tasks API covering 200+ formats. {product} uses the same jobs/tasks model and similar format coverage ({formats} formats, {conversions} directions), and adds what a pure converter doesn't do: editing the file by instruction, recognising and filling forms, signatures, and an MCP server for AI assistants.
faq: Is {product} a CloudConvert alternative?
Yes: a jobs/tasks REST API with import, convert and export tasks, webhooks and sandbox keys, plus the browser converter — and AI editing, forms and signatures on top.
Can I move my CloudConvert jobs over?
The job JSON is very close: named tasks with operation, input and output_format. Most jobs need only the base URL and the key changed.

freeconvert.name: FreeConvert
freeconvert.desc: Many browser converters; {product} adds AI editing, forms, signatures and MCP.
freeconvert.intro: FreeConvert offers a large set of browser converters and compressors with advanced options. {product} matches the conversion and option range ({formats} formats, presets, apply-to-all) and adds AI editing, form recognition, signatures and MCP.
faq: Does {product} have the same advanced video options?
Yes: codec, CRF, bitrate, resolution, aspect ratio, frame rate, trim, rotate, flip, subtitles and volume — and allow-listed FFmpeg parameters.

smallpdf.name: Smallpdf
smallpdf.desc: PDF tools with e-sign; {product} covers {formats} formats and edits by instruction.
smallpdf.intro: Smallpdf focuses on PDF tools and e-signatures. {product} has the PDF suite (merge, split, compress, protect, OCR, PDF/A, sign) and goes beyond PDFs: {formats} formats, video and audio, AI editing of Word and PowerPoint files, form recognition from photos, and MCP.
faq: Can I sign PDFs as with Smallpdf?
Yes: draw or photograph your signature once, it is stored encrypted and placed into PDF or Word files — also by your AI assistant.

ilovepdf.name: iLovePDF
ilovepdf.desc: PDF tools with an API; {product} adds all other formats, AI editing and MCP.
ilovepdf.intro: iLovePDF is a popular PDF toolkit with an API and e-signatures. {product} offers the same PDF operations and an API, plus {formats} formats beyond PDF, AI editing, agentic form filling and an MCP server.
faq: Is there a Hungarian interface?
Yes, {product} is fully available in Hungarian and English, and a new language is one translation file.

dev.title: {product} API — file conversion, tools, forms and signatures
dev.desc: REST API for {formats} file formats: jobs and tasks, webhooks, sandbox keys, OpenAPI, SDKs for Python and Node, Zapier, Make and n8n.
dev.lead: One REST API for {formats} formats, {conversions} conversion directions and {tools} tools. Jobs are made of named tasks (import → convert or tool → export) that run in parallel where they can; you follow them live (long-poll or Server-Sent Events) or by webhook. Default limit: {rate} requests per minute per key.
dev.docs_p: Authentication, jobs, uploads, live status, webhooks, sandbox, limits and every operation.
dev.jb_p: Build a job visually and copy it as JSON or curl.
dev.mcp_p: Connect Claude or ChatGPT to the same tools over MCP.
dev.openapi_p: The machine-readable spec for code generators.
dev.sdk_p: Python (sdk/python) and Node (sdk/node) SDKs, Zapier, Make and n8n integrations ship in the repository and need only the base URL and a key.

docs.title: {product} API documentation
docs.desc: How to use the {product} REST API: keys, jobs and tasks, uploads, status, webhooks, sandbox and limits, with curl, Python and JavaScript.
docs.lead: Everything to integrate in an afternoon. Default rate limit: {rate} requests per minute per key.
docs.auth_p: Create a key in the app under Connect your AI → API keys and send it as a Bearer token. Keys starting with sk_test_ are sandbox keys: they don't use credits.
docs.jobs_p: A job is a set of named tasks. A task's input is the name of an earlier task (or a list of names). Tasks without dependencies start immediately and in parallel.
docs.upload_p: Use an import/upload task: its result gives a one-time upload URL. Large files can be sent in chunks of up to 50 MB each.
docs.status_p: Poll the job with ?wait=N (long-poll up to 60 s) or open the Server-Sent Events stream for task.updated, job.finished and job.failed events.
docs.webhooks_p: Register a URL for job.finished and job.failed, or give webhook_url per job. Every delivery is signed with HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp and body; failed deliveries are retried three times.
docs.sandbox_p: Sandbox keys (sk_test_…) run real conversions on files up to 10 MB without using credits; results are kept for one hour. Use them for development and CI.
docs.limits_p: Default {rate} requests per minute per key (HTTP 429 with Retry-After beyond). Tasks count against the monthly task allowance of your plan; above it, 1 credit per 20 tasks. AI tasks (OCR by vision model, form recognition from photos, agentic filling) use the existing page allowances.

jb.title: Job Builder — build {product} API jobs visually
jb.desc: Assemble import, convert, tool and export tasks and copy the job as JSON or curl, or run it with a sandbox key.
jb.lead: Add tasks, set their fields, and copy the JSON or the curl command — or run it right here with a sandbox key.

api.title: {src} to {dst} API — convert {src} to {dst} with a REST call
api.desc: Convert {src} to {dst} programmatically: one REST job with import, convert and export tasks; curl, Python and JavaScript examples.
api.lead: Send a {src} file and get {dst} back with one job: import the file, convert it ({engines}), export a download link. Webhooks and live status included; default limit {rate} requests per minute.

cai.title: Connect your AI to {product} — MCP for Claude and ChatGPT
cai.desc: Give Claude, ChatGPT and other AI assistants every converter, tool, form and signature function of {product} over MCP.
cai.lead: {product} is an MCP server with {n} grouped tools. Connect it once and your assistant converts, edits, fills and signs files for you — and every result comes back with a download and an editor link.
cai.url_p: Streamable HTTP. Sign in with OAuth when the client asks, or create a personal key in the app (Connect your AI → API keys) and send it as Authorization: Bearer <key>.
cai.claude1: In Claude open Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector.
cai.claude3: Sign in and allow access — the tools appear in the chat.
cai.gpt1: In ChatGPT open Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced → Developer mode.
cai.gpt2: Create a connector with the URL {url}.
faq: Which assistants work?
Any MCP client with Streamable HTTP: Claude (web, desktop, Claude Code), ChatGPT developer mode and Apps, Cursor, and others.
Does the assistant see my other files?
Only through the tools, only in your own workspace, and only when you ask it to; you can revoke access in the app at any time.
Can the assistant ask me for missing form data?
Yes. During agentic form filling it asks for missing values through MCP elicitation when the client supports it, otherwise in the chat.
